page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u0.c1m2.2xlarge is an x86_64 compute-oriented virtual server operating on the KVM hypervisor. The instance features 8 dedicated virtual central processing units and 16.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 compute-optimized ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The machine contains no graphics processing units and includes no local physical disk storage, relying entirely on network-attached cloud disks for persistent storage and operating system volumes.

Network connectivity features a baseline throughput of 2 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are bundled with the instance. A technical tradeoff exists regarding the absence of onboard storage and moderate baseline network capacity, making external disk performance dependent on remote network latency. Qualitatively, allocating less RAM per vCPU without bundled local NVMe media offers cost efficiency for processor-centric tasks that do not demand extensive memory buffers.

The hardware profile aligns with compute-intensive tasks operating within a restrained memory footprint. Best-fit use cases include distributed compilation nodes, continuous integration and continuous deployment workers, batch data pipelines, background queue processing, and microservice backend components requiring dedicated CPU allocation.

It provides 8 dedicated vCPUs paired with 16.0 GB of RAM, allocating 2.0 GB per core. The server includes no GPUs and omits local storage, necessitating reliance on network-attached storage volumes for all file system and persistent disk operations. Network performance is provisioned with a 2 Gbps baseline bandwidth, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned. Economically, this resource footprint provides an efficient framework for CPU-bound tasks by minimizing redundant memory overhead and excluding premium bundled NVMe media. The primary operational tradeoff involves reliance on remote network volumes for persistent storage alongside constrained networking capacity. The server fits batch processing pipelines, build and continuous integration environments, worker queues, and compute-driven microservices.
